body:
The global data center market size was valued at USD 269.79 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow from USD 300.64 billion in 2026 to USD 699.13 billion by 2034, exhibiting a CAGR of 11.10% during the forecast period. North America dominated the global data center market, accounting for 38.50% market share in 2025. Industry growth is driven by hyperscale expansion, AI infrastructure demand, accelerated cloud adoption, and enterprise digital transformation investments across emerging and [...] The market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 11.10% during the forecast period.

By data center type, the colocation segment is expected to lead the market.

Increased digitalization and cloud adoption among industries drive market growth.

Schneider Electric, ABB Ltd., IBM Corporation, Cisco System, Inc., Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., and Hitachi Ltd are the top players in the market.

North America held the highest market share in 2024. [...] North America leads the global data center market due to hyperscale concentration, mature cloud adoption, and deep capital availability. Strong fiber connectivity, renewable procurement frameworks, and enterprise outsourcing support sustained capacity expansion. Power constraints in key metropolitan hubs influence site selection toward secondary markets. The region maintains a dominant market share, supported by long-term hyperscale lease commitments.

## 7. Phoenix

Offering lower taxes, affordable power and real estate, robust fiber and cable connectivity and minimal exposure to natural disasters, Phoenix is another top data center market in the U.S., with 170+ data centers ready to serve the area. Arizona also offers a reliable power grid with access to renewable energy sources, a plus for organizations committed to sustainability efforts.

## 8. Atlanta [...] Located between two of the largest data center markets in the U.S. — Northern Virginia and Silicon Valley — Dallas features more than 200 data centers. Its central location, power costs well below the national average and affordable real estate costs vs. other U.S. data center markets are key drivers within the data center marketplace. With both metro and long-haul connectivity as well as a strong economy, Dallas offers a sound, affordable alternative to higher-priced West Coast data centers. [...] ## 8. Atlanta

With the third-largest concentration of Fortune 500 companies in the U.S., Atlanta is one of the fastest-growing data center markets in the country. The city's more than 150 data centers host prosperous technology, health, digital media, transportation and security companies, in addition to industry giants such as Coca-Cola, Delta Airlines, UPS, Georgia-Pacific and Cox Enterprises.
